title: Expanding brackets: why 3(x + 2) is 3x + 6

explain.say: Picture 3 party bags in Mexico City. Each bag has x sweets and 2 lollipops. Let us say x is 4. See the 3 groups on the board? Each has 4 plus 2, which is 6 things. We write this as 3 bracket x plus 2.
First count the sweets. There are x sweets in each of 3 bags. That is 3x. With x as 4, look at the array: 3 rows of 4 is 12 sweets.
Now count the lollipops. 2 in each of 3 bags. That is 3 times 2, which is 6. See the 3 rows of 2? Did you remember the lollipops?
Put them together: 3x plus 6. With x as 4, that is 12 plus 6, which is 18. And the whole array, 3 rows of 6, is also 18. It matches! The 3 multiplies everything inside the bracket.

Great job! Look at the 3 bags again. A common slip is to write 3x plus 2 and forget the lollipops. Wow: this rule, called the distributive law, helps you do 3 times 102 in your head: 300 plus 6. Challenge: expand 5 bracket y minus 3.

faq.q: What does a number outside a bracket mean?
faq.a: It means multiply everything inside by that number. 3 bracket x plus 2 means 3 lots of x plus 2.

faq.q: Why isn't 3 bracket x plus 2 equal to 3x plus 2?
faq.a: Each of the 3 bags has its own 2 lollipops. So there are 3 times 2, which is 6 lollipops, not just 2.
asks: Why does the 3 multiply both terms?

faq.q: How do you check an expansion?
faq.a: Pick a number for x and work out both sides. If x is 4, 3 times 6 and 12 plus 6 both give 18.
asks: How do I know my expansion is right?

faq.q: How do you expand 5 bracket y minus 3?
faq.a: Multiply both terms by 5. 5 times y is 5y, and 5 times minus 3 is minus 15. So it is 5y minus 15.

faq.q: What is the opposite of expanding brackets?
faq.a: Factorising. It puts the brackets back, so 3x plus 6 becomes 3 bracket x plus 2.
asks: How do you put brackets back in?

facts: Expanding brackets uses the distributive law: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Factorising is the reverse of expanding: 3x + 6 = 3(x + 2).

wrong.2: This forgets to multiply the a.

quiz.why: 2 times 3x is 6x, and 2 times minus 1 is minus 2.

wrong.2: This adds 2 to 3x instead of multiplying.
